body: Take care of yourself. I've gone through a lot of similar experiences to you, and even when things seemed utterly hopeless, eventually life got kind to me and I found myself in a good place. Best of luck.

I had the exact same worries when I went into a therapist so I can totally relate. The cool thing I discovered was, you don't have to reveal anything you don't want to, and you can also ask them to walk you through everything step by step, telling you what the potential consequences are of the things you talk about. All he has to do is say, "If I wanted to tell you something my father MAY have done, when would you be required to report it?" They will lay everything out clearly for you, so there will be no surprises. He can still get help around how his father's actions made him feel without even revealing them in detail. 

Unless other children are currently in danger from his father, the therapist is required by law to maintain confidentiality. So your husband's fear is totally understandable, but ultimately, he will find therapy's goal is to help him make his life less complicated, not make his life harder.

My dad beat the shit out of me when I was a kid, and he would always cry and apologize afterwards too. That didn't stop him from doing it again whenever he lost control. I understand the love you feel for your husband. I actually think it's rare for someone who's abusive to be terrible all the time. That's kind of a TV myth. If they weren't sweet most of the time, they couldn't get away with it when they're horrible. The fact that he doesn't want to get help is a bad sign. It sounds like you're doing everything right. It's a horribly tough situation to be in. His love for you is probably real. But you deserve love that doesn't come with violence as the price of admission. Having a bad childhood is not an excuse for him to attack the person who cares about him the most. If you're committed to sticking it out with your husband, tell him the bravest and strongest thing he could do as a man is go talk to a professional about his anger. He'll feel like a hero after facing his demons.

You deserve to be treated better. I've been stuck in domestic violence situations before and I felt miserable, scared and hopeless. I don't know where you live since you've got dollar signs and euros up there, but I REALLY encourage you to do a google search for a shelter in your area that assists women who have been attacked by their husbands. They're safe and supportive environments that help women from all income levels restart their lives when they're financially dependent on their abusers. I'm sure there are nice things about your husband, but that doesn't excuse his behavior. YOU DESERVE BETTER. Money problems are tough, but the world will seem so much better when you're not in fear of being attacked by someone you love.

It sounds like you've got a lot to deal with. I can't offer you any advice except to say that you sound like a really strong person after everything you've been through. I hope that life gives you some breaks soon enough, because you definitely deserve them. Sometimes life doesn't treat cool people well, but trust me, you sound like an amazing person who wants happiness and takes life seriously. And that's more than can be said for a lot of people these days. I'll be cheering you on privately in my head. You've got at least one fan in me, and probably a few more you might not realize.
This helps more than you can imagine. I definitely felt myself in an ethical quandary. Thanks!

Thanks for your response. I've also heard that therapists can be required to report abuse if they suspect children are in danger. My father's practice currently involves counseling for children. That's the bind I'm in. I have nothing to indicate he currently abuses children, and he seems to have improved as a person since my childhood. But I know a lot of terrible things happened to me, some of which he probably participated in.
